Hours in New Schedule

(Based on 135 meetings of ~58.5 min avg.)

The new schedule results in a very slight decrease in total annual contact time compared to a typical block schedule. The key challenge is adapting to fewer, but more frequent, class meetings per week.

Deconstructing the 8-Drop-2 Schedule

The new schedule operates on a 4-day rotation. This means any given class will meet 3 times within that 4-day cycle. Over a standard 5-day school week, this most frequently results in 3 or 4 class meetings, ensuring consistent contact time.

Week-by-Week Curriculum Map

First Quarter

Week 1 (Aug 28-29)

Rotation: Day 1, Day 2

Unit 1: Course Intro, Lab Safety, Scientific Method.

Weeks 2-3 (Sep 1-12)

Rotation: Day 3 → Day 3

Unit 1: Energy Systems. Transition to Unit 2: Kinematics (Speed, Velocity, Displacement). Graphing motion.

Assessment: Unit 1 Test

Weeks 4-5 (Sep 15-26)

Rotation: Day 4 → Day 4

Unit 2: Accelerated Motion and Freefall. In-depth problem-solving.

Weeks 6-7 (Sep 29 - Oct 10)

Rotation: Day 1 → Day 2

Unit 3: Intro to Vectors & Trigonometry. Vector addition and components.

Assessment: Kinematics (Unit 2) Test

Weeks 8-9 (Oct 13-24)

Rotation: Day 3 → Day 3

Unit 3: Vector Resolution and introduction to 2D Kinematics (Projectile Motion).

Week 10 (Oct 27-31)

Rotation: Day 4 → Day 3

Unit 3: Projectile Motion Lab and applications.

Second Quarter

Weeks 11-12 (Nov 3-14)

Rotation: Day 4 → Day 4

Unit 3: Relative Motion & Review. Transition to Unit 4: Dynamics (Newton's Laws).

Assessment: Vectors/2D Kinematics (Unit 3) Test

Weeks 13-15 (Nov 17 - Dec 5)

Rotation: Day 1 → Day 4

Unit 4: Free Body Diagrams, Net Force, and Friction.

Weeks 16-18 (Dec 8 - Jan 9)

Rotation: Day 1 → Day 1

Unit 4: Inclined Planes. Unit Review. Transition to Unit 5: Work & Energy.

Assessment: Dynamics (Unit 4) Test

Weeks 19-20 (Jan 12-23)

Rotation: Day 2 → Day 2

Unit 5: Work-Energy Theorem, Conservation of Energy, Power. Midterm Prep.

Assessment: Midterm Exams
